title: Concept Vector Similarity Across Independently Trained Models of the Same Architecture

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain: if concept vectors converge across training runs, a single extraction suffices for all models of that architecture. Interesting scientific question with practical implications but somewhat niche.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Obtaining two independently trained instances of the same architecture is the main barrier. Pre-trained checkpoints with different random seeds are rarely publicly available for large models. Training from scratch is far beyond medium compute. This may be infeasible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: If suitable model pairs exist, the experiment itself is focused: extract vectors from both, compute cosine similarity. But finding appropriate model pairs could consume much of the time budget. Moderate scope if feasibility is resolved.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
